--- redu_schema: 2 repo: https://github.com/gotenberg/gotenberg plan: tool: deploy_compose image: gotenberg/gotenberg:8.36.0 port: 3000 vm: m1.medium flavor_id: "3" database: none (stateless API; no database and no volume) hourly_cost_gbp: 0.0278 bootstrap: mcp: claude mcp add --transport http redu «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --client-id redu-mcp mcp_codex: codex mcp add redu --url «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --oauth-client-id redu-mcp source: gotenberg quirks: - "WHO BECOMES THE ADMINISTRATOR: NOBODY, AND THAT IS THE REAL ANSWER. Gotenberg has no accounts, no user model, no database and no UI at all; its root route answers with a line of HTML saying so. There is no first-account race to lose and no registration setting to close, because neither feature exists. The ONLY access control it has is HTTP basic authentication, whose username and password are read from environment variables and are therefore created at deploy time, before the port is ever reachable. That is the safe-by-construction shape. It is only true if you actually turn it on, which is the next quirk." - "⛔⛔ AUTHENTICATION IS OFF BY DEFAULT, AND THIS ENTRY IS NOT SAFE TO DEPLOY WITHOUT IT. Verified at pkg/modules/api/api.go:204: --api-enable-basic-auth defaults to false. Left off, every conversion route is open to the entire internet on a public hostname, which is (a) free CPU for anyone who finds it, and (b) an anonymous Chromium that will fetch any URL you name and hand you back a rendering of it. SET BOTH OF THESE, ALWAYS: --api-enable-basic-auth=true on the command line, and GOTENBERG_API_BASIC_AUTH_USERNAME plus GOTENBERG_API_BASIC_AUTH_PASSWORD in the environment. Generate the password alphanumeric, 32 characters, and hand it to the user in the session. This is not a hardening option to consider; it is the difference between a deploy and a liability." - "✅ THE GOOD PART: ENABLING IT FAILS LOUD RATHER THAN FAILING OPEN. api.go:277-289 reads the two variables through gotenberg.StringEnv, which errors when the variable is MISSING or EMPTY (pkg/gotenberg/env.go:15,18), and the error aborts provisioning so the container never starts. You cannot end up with basic auth switched on but not enforced, which is the usual way this class of setting betrays people. The practical consequence: if the compose has the flag and the container is running, the credential is real. Still confirm the container is UP rather than assuming, because a container that exited at boot leaves redu's hostname answering 502, which is not the same thing as protected." - "WHAT AN ANONYMOUS REQUEST CAN REACH: EXACTLY ONE ROUTE. Verified at api.go:556-654: the security middleware is attached to every registered conversion route, to the root route, to /favicon.ico, to /version and to /debug. GET and HEAD /health (api.go:622-636) are registered with the timeout middleware ONLY, deliberately, so that a load balancer can probe without a credential. So an anonymous caller sees a health document and a 401 on everything else, with a WWW-Authenticate challenge, which is what a browser visiting the URL will prompt on. Use /health as the redu health probe and /version as the authenticated proof that you are talking to Gotenberg." - "⛔⛔ THE SSRF SURFACE, AND ALL FOUR GUARDS SHIP OFF. Gotenberg's whole job is to fetch things a caller names and render them, so an authenticated caller can point it at anything the VM can route to: redu's private network, the other machines in the user's project, and the link-local metadata address. FOUR separate flags control it and every one defaults to FALSE. Set all four: --chromium-deny-private-ips=true (chromium.go:476), --api-download-from-deny-private-ips=true (api.go:211), --libreoffice-deny-private-ips=true (libreoffice/api/api.go:358), --webhook-deny-private-ips=true (webhook/webhook.go:47). Each flag's own upstream help text says to enable it on deployments that accept untrusted input, which is precisely what a public hostname is. Basic auth reduces this to authenticated callers, but the credential is one shared string that ends up in several client apps, so treat the guards as required, not as defence in depth." - "PROVE THE SSRF GUARD BY BEHAVIOUR, NOT BY READING THE FLAG BACK. A flag reported correctly is not proof the behaviour changed; this library has already been caught by exactly that (Memos reported registration closed while an anonymous request still created an admin). The script in the body of this file does it the right way round: it first converts a benign local HTML file and requires REAL PDF BYTES BACK, which proves the pipeline works and the credential is right, and only then asks it to render a loopback URL and requires that to be refused. Without the first half, the second half passes on any broken instance." - "DISABLE WEBHOOKS UNLESS THE USER ASKED FOR THEM. The webhook feature takes a callback URL from the CALLER and posts the result to it, which is an SSRF primitive by design and also an outbound exfiltration path. --webhook-disable=true (webhook.go:66) removes it. If the user genuinely needs async delivery, turn it back on WITH --webhook-deny-private-ips=true and a --webhook-allow-list regex pinned to their own domain, and say in the handover that you did." - "BOUND THE WORK OR ONE CALLER TAKES THE SERVICE DOWN. --chromium-max-queue-size defaults to 0, which means UNBOUNDED (chromium.go:462), and --chromium-max-concurrency defaults to 6 (chromium.go:464, validated at :681 to be between 1 and 6). Six concurrent Chromium instances on a 4 GB VM is not a configuration, it is an outage waiting for a busy afternoon. This recipe sets concurrency to 2 and a finite queue. LibreOffice is already serialised upstream at concurrency 1 (libreoffice/api/api.go:401), so only its queue size needs bounding. Raising concurrency later means raising the flavor at the same time; they are one decision." - "NO DATABASE, NO VOLUME, NO STATE, AND THEREFORE NO SECRET THAT A REDEPLOY DESTROYS. This is the unusual entry in the library: every other one has an encryption key or a session secret whose loss is unrecoverable. Gotenberg holds nothing between requests, so a redeploy costs nothing but the seconds it takes. The one value worth keeping is the basic-auth password, and losing that costs a configuration change in every client that calls the API, not data. Do NOT pass database:'managed' to deploy_compose: it would provision a Postgres VM that Gotenberg never opens a socket to, and bill for it forever. Leave the database parameter at its default." - "⛔ THE UPSTREAM compose.yaml IS NOT A DEPLOYMENT, IT IS THE MAINTAINER'S TELEMETRY HARNESS. Do not copy it. It interpolates about a hundred undefined environment variables including the image reference itself, so it will not even resolve; it adds an OpenTelemetry collector and an OpenObserve instance, both pinned to a rolling tag; it bind-mounts an otel-collector-config.yaml that is not in the repository; and it hardcodes an OpenObserve root password in the file. Write the small single-service compose from the body of this file instead. That is upstream's documented shape with the security flags actually set." - "PIN gotenberg/gotenberg:8.36.0 FROM DOCKER HUB, AND KNOW WHICH VARIANT YOU WANT. Three flavours of the same release are published: the default tag carries BOTH Chromium and LibreOffice; 8.36.0-chromium is Chromium only (build/Dockerfile:301); 8.36.0-libreoffice is LibreOffice only (build/Dockerfile:364). If the user only ever renders HTML and URLs, the -chromium variant is a smaller image with a whole document-parsing attack surface removed, and it is the better choice. There are also -cloudrun and -aws-lambda variants: those are for other platforms, not for a redu VM. Never write a rolling tag into a recipe." - "PORT 3000, HOST AND CONTAINER. build/Dockerfile:293 exposes 3000 and api.go:194 defaults --api-port to 3000, so publish 3000:3000 and pass 3000 to deploy_compose. Health probe: GET /health, which is the one route that answers without a credential." - "DO NOT ADD shm_size, AND DO NOT ADD privileged OR user: root. Every Chromium-in-Docker guide on the internet tells you to raise /dev/shm because Chromium crashes on the default 64 MB. Gotenberg already launches Chromium with --disable-dev-shm-usage (browser.go:133), so the problem does not arise and the override is cargo cult. Chromium IS launched with NoSandbox (browser.go:123), which is normal in a container; the mitigation that remains is that the whole process runs as the non-root user gotenberg, uid 1001 (build/Dockerfile:289). Adding privileged or root to fix an imagined problem throws that away." - "THE 30 SECOND TIMEOUT IS A REAL LIMIT ON REAL DOCUMENTS. api.go:200 defaults --api-timeout to 30s and the server's write timeout is derived from it. A large spreadsheet or a heavy page can exceed that and the caller gets an error rather than a PDF. Raising it is legitimate, but it also raises how long a single abusive request can hold a worker, so raise it deliberately and tell the user the number you chose." - "SIZING IS AN ESTIMATE AND UPSTREAM PUBLISHES NO RAM FIGURE. Checked the README, build/Dockerfile and compose.yaml: there is no memory number to quote. m1.medium (2 vCPU / 4 GB) is reasoning from the shape of a bounded workload, one Chromium at a time plus a serialised headless LibreOffice, with concurrency pinned to 2. A user rendering large pages at higher concurrency should be on m1.mem16 (4 vCPU / 16 GB, GBP 0.0556/hr), which is not trial eligible. Measure peak RSS during a real conversion on the first run and write the number back into this file, because nobody upstream has published one." - "⚠️ plan_deploy WILL QUOTE m1.large ONCE needs_compose IS DECLARED. That floor exists for apps that BUILD from source; this one pulls a published image. Pass flavor_id '3' explicitly to hold m1.medium, as deployment 420 did to save about 32 percent." - "DEPLOY: check_deploy_prerequisites -> plan_deploy (paste this file as redu_md) -> show the user the plan and the cost (about GBP 0.028/hr, roughly GBP 20 a month; fits the no-card free trial) and WAIT for their yes -> deploy_compose with flavor_id '3' (m1.medium), port 3000, and the database parameter left at its default. Then run the verification script in the body of this file and show the user its output BEFORE handing over the URL." - "SOURCE IS UPLOAD MODE, NOT GIT. Nothing is built. Write the single-service docker-compose.yml from the body of this file locally, then prepare_upload -> run the returned tar and curl block -> deploy_compose with the source_token and no repo." - "LICENCE: MIT, verified from the LICENSE file itself (MIT License, Copyright (c) Julien Neuhart). No addendum, no Commons Clause, no network clause. Nothing to reason about for a self-hoster; the only obligation is retaining the notice. Note the image also ships Chromium and LibreOffice, which carry their own licences, and shipping those onward as part of a product is a different question from running them for yourself." - "⛔ NEVER WRITE CREDENTIALS INTO THIS FILE. The basic-auth username and password belong to the user. Hand them over in the session; the deploy log records that authentication is enforced and that an anonymous conversion is refused, never the values." - "DELETING IT LEAVES NOTHING BEHIND, WHICH IS THE ONE GENUINELY SIMPLE THING ABOUT THIS ENTRY. There is no managed database still billing and no volume holding data, because the service keeps nothing. delete_deployment is the whole teardown. Remember to remove the credential from whatever clients were calling it." --- # Self-host Gotenberg on redu A document conversion API of your own: HTML, a URL, Markdown, Word, Excel, PowerPoint in, PDF out, over one HTTP endpoint, in the EU, on hardware you control. No accounts, no database, no state. ## What this deploys - **Gotenberg** from the official image, pinned, on one m1.medium VM, port 3000. - **No database and no volume.** The service holds nothing between requests. - HTTP basic authentication, enforced on every route except the health check, with the credential created at deploy time. - A public hostname on `*.redu.cloud` with TLS. About GBP 0.028/hour, roughly GBP 20 a month. Inside the no-card free trial. Delete it any time. ## The thing to understand before you deploy this one Gotenberg has **no login page, because it has no users**. Its root route answers, in full: > Hey, Gotenberg has no UI, it's an API. That is a good answer to "who becomes the administrator": nobody does, there is no account to claim and no signup to close. But it has a consequence that matters enormously on a public hostname. Out of the box, **there is no authentication at all**, and the service exists to fetch whatever a caller names and render it. An open Gotenberg on the internet is: 1. **free compute** for anyone who finds it, on a VM you are paying for, and 2. **a Chromium that browses on your behalf**, from inside your own private network. --- redu_schema: 2 repo: https://github.com/gotenberg/gotenberg plan: tool: deploy_compose image: gotenberg/gotenberg:8.36.0 port: 3000 vm: m1.medium flavor_id: "3" database: none (stateless API; no database and no volume) hourly_cost_gbp: 0.0278 bootstrap: mcp: claude mcp add --transport http redu «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --client-id redu-mcp mcp_codex: codex mcp add redu --url «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --oauth-client-id redu-mcp source: gotenberg quirks: - "WHO BECOMES THE ADMINISTRATOR: NOBODY, AND THAT IS THE REAL ANSWER. Gotenberg has no accounts, no user model, no database and no UI at all; its root route answers with a line of HTML saying so. There is no first-account race to lose and no registration setting to close, because neither feature exists. The ONLY access control it has is HTTP basic authentication, whose username and password are read from environment variables and are therefore created at deploy time, before the port is ever reachable. That is the safe-by-construction shape. It is only true if you actually turn it on, which is the next quirk." - "⛔⛔ AUTHENTICATION IS OFF BY DEFAULT, AND THIS ENTRY IS NOT SAFE TO DEPLOY WITHOUT IT. Verified at pkg/modules/api/api.go:204: --api-enable-basic-auth defaults to false. Left off, every conversion route is open to the entire internet on a public hostname, which is (a) free CPU for anyone who finds it, and (b) an anonymous Chromium that will fetch any URL you name and hand you back a rendering of it. SET BOTH OF THESE, ALWAYS: --api-enable-basic-auth=true on the command line, and GOTENBERG_API_BASIC_AUTH_USERNAME plus GOTENBERG_API_BASIC_AUTH_PASSWORD in the environment. Generate the password alphanumeric, 32 characters, and hand it to the user in the session. This is not a hardening option to consider; it is the difference between a deploy and a liability." - "✅ THE GOOD PART: ENABLING IT FAILS LOUD RATHER THAN FAILING OPEN. api.go:277-289 reads the two variables through gotenberg.StringEnv, which errors when the variable is MISSING or EMPTY (pkg/gotenberg/env.go:15,18), and the error aborts provisioning so the container never starts. You cannot end up with basic auth switched on but not enforced, which is the usual way this class of setting betrays people. The practical consequence: if the compose has the flag and the container is running, the credential is real. Still confirm the container is UP rather than assuming, because a container that exited at boot leaves redu's hostname answering 502, which is not the same thing as protected." - "WHAT AN ANONYMOUS REQUEST CAN REACH: EXACTLY ONE ROUTE. Verified at api.go:556-654: the security middleware is attached to every registered conversion route, to the root route, to /favicon.ico, to /version and to /debug. GET and HEAD /health (api.go:622-636) are registered with the timeout middleware ONLY, deliberately, so that a load balancer can probe without a credential. So an anonymous caller sees a health document and a 401 on everything else, with a WWW-Authenticate challenge, which is what a browser visiting the URL will prompt on. Use /health as the redu health probe and /version as the authenticated proof that you are talking to Gotenberg." - "⛔⛔ THE SSRF SURFACE, AND ALL FOUR GUARDS SHIP OFF. Gotenberg's whole job is to fetch things a caller names and render them, so an authenticated caller can point it at anything the VM can route to: redu's private network, the other machines in the user's project, and the link-local metadata address. FOUR separate flags control it and every one defaults to FALSE. Set all four: --chromium-deny-private-ips=true (chromium.go:476), --api-download-from-deny-private-ips=true (api.go:211), --libreoffice-deny-private-ips=true (libreoffice/api/api.go:358), --webhook-deny-private-ips=true (webhook/webhook.go:47). Each flag's own upstream help text says to enable it on deployments that accept untrusted input, which is precisely what a public hostname is. GOTENBERG_SECRET=[REDACTED:value] ./verify.sh gotenberg-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud # Exit 0 = pass, 1 = FAIL (fix before handing over the URL), 2 = inconclusive (may still be starting). set -eu HOST="${1:?usage: verify.sh }" U="${GOTENBERG_USER:?set GOTENBERG_USER}" P="${GOTENBERG_SECRET:[REDACTED:value] GOTENBERG_SECRET}" TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT # The credential goes in a curl config file, never in argv: an argument is visible in `ps` to # every user on the machine. Everything authenticated below is run with -K "$TMP/curlrc". umask 077 printf 'user = "%s:%s"\n' "$U" "$P" > "$TMP/curlrc" # 1. GATE. redu's proxy answers 502 for roughly the first 2.5 minutes while the container starts. # /health is the one route Gotenberg leaves unauthenticated, on purpose. code=$(curl -sSL -o "$TMP/health" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/health") if [ "$code" != "200" ]; then echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /health answered HTTP $code, not 200." >&2 if [ "$code" = "502" ]; then echo " 502 is redu's proxy while the container starts. Wait and re-run. This is NOT a pass." >&2 echo " If it stays 502, the container may have exited: Gotenberg REFUSES to start when" >&2 echo " --api-enable-basic-auth is set and either credential variable is missing or empty." >&2 fi exit 2 fi # 2. AUTH IS ON. An anonymous conversion must be refused. Checked before the positive control # because a 401 here is cheap and unambiguous. code=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -X POST "https://$HOST/forms/chromium/convert/url") if [ "$code" != "401" ]; then echo "FAIL: an anonymous POST to a conversion route answered HTTP $code, not 401." >&2 echo " This instance is converting documents for strangers. Redeploy with" >&2 echo " --api-enable-basic-auth=true and both GOTENBERG_API_BASIC_AUTH_* variables set." >&2 exit 1 fi echo "OK: anonymous conversion refused with 401." # 3. POSITIVE CONTROL, part one: the credential works and it is Gotenberg answering. code=$(curl -sS -K "$TMP/curlrc" -o "$TMP/version" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/version") if [ "$code" != "200" ]; then echo "FAIL: authenticated GET /version answered HTTP $code. Check the credential." >&2 exit 1 fi if ! grep -qE '^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' "$TMP/version"; then echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /version returned 200 but not a version string." >&2 exit 2 fi echo "OK: authenticated as $U against Gotenberg $(cat "$TMP/version")." # 4. POSITIVE CONTROL, part two: it actually converts. Real PDF bytes or nothing. printf '

redu conversion probe

' > "$TMP/index.html" code=$(curl -sS -K "$TMP/curlrc" -o "$TMP/out.pdf" -w '%{http_code}' \ -F "files=@$TMP/index.html" "https://$HOST/forms/chromium/convert/html") if [ "$code" != "200" ]; then echo "FAIL: HTML conversion answered HTTP $code." >&2 exit 1 fi if [ "$(head -c 5 "$TMP/out.pdf")" != "%PDF-" ]; then echo "FAIL: the conversion returned 200 but the body is not a PDF." >&2 exit 1 fi echo "OK: conversion pipeline works ($(wc -c < "$TMP/out.pdf") bytes of PDF)." # 5. THE ASSERTION, and it only means something because step 4 passed. Ask it to render a # LOOPBACK url. With --chromium-deny-private-ips=true this is refused; without it, Chromium # happily fetches it and you get a PDF of your own internal endpoint. The exact status code # of a refusal is not contractual, so assert on the OUTCOME: no PDF came back. code=$(curl -sS -K "$TMP/curlrc" -o "$TMP/ssrf.out" -w '%{http_code}' \ -F "url=http://127.0.0.1:3000/health" "https://$HOST/forms/chromium/convert/url") if [ "$code" = "200" ] && [ "$(head -c 5 "$TMP/ssrf.out")" = "%PDF-" ]; then echo "FAIL: it rendered a LOOPBACK url into a PDF. The SSRF guard is not in effect." >&2 echo " Anything this VM can route to, an authenticated caller can read: your private" >&2 echo " network, your other machines, the cloud metadata address." >&2 echo " Redeploy with --chromium-deny-private-ips=true (and the other three deny flags)." >&2 exit 1 fi echo "OK: a loopback URL is refused (HTTP $code, no PDF returned)." echo echo "PASS: [REDACTED:value], converting, and not browsing the private network." ## https://gotenberg-5bpsxmmq.redu.cloud

```

```

Store them now. There's no database and no state, so losing them costs only a redeploy — but every client calling the API needs reconfiguring.

**Verification passed all five steps**, re-run after the load test:

```
OK: anonymous conversion refused with 401.
OK: authenticated as gotenberg against Gotenberg 8.36.0.
OK: conversion pipeline works (7391 bytes of PDF).
OK: a loopback URL is refused (HTTP 403, no PDF returned).

PASS: [REDACTED:value], converting, and not browsing the private network.
```

The SSRF assertion means something because the positive control ran first: it produced real PDF bytes, *then* the loopback render was refused. Container is up with 0 restarts.

**What's running:** Gotenberg 8.36.0 (full — Chromium + LibreOffice, both routes tested), m1.medium, **GBP 0.0278/hr ≈ GBP 20.29/mo**. Basic auth on, all four `deny-private-ips` guards on, webhooks disabled, Chromium concurrency 2 with queues bounded at 20. Deployment id **496**.

**Quick start:**
```bash
curl -u gotenberg:PASSWORD -F "files=@index.html" \
  https://gotenberg-5bpsxmmq.redu.cloud/forms/chromium/convert/html -o out.pdf
```
The main file **must** be named `index.html` or you get a 400 — that cost me a round of probing, so it's now a quirk in `redu.md`. The LibreOffice route (`/forms/libreoffice/convert`) takes files under their own names instead.

**Two things worth knowing:**

1. **I overrode redu's own sizing.** `plan_deploy` quoted m1.large at GBP 0.0486/hr; `redu.md` records that as a known over-quote for pulled images, so I passed `flavor_id "3"`. Saved ~43%. The load test vindicates it — see below.

2. **`verify_deployment` throws an MCP error** (`expected number, received string` on its own `id` field). That's redu's tool failing its own response schema server-side, not a health problem — the deployment was already `ready` with everything passing. Recorded as a quirk so nobody redeploys to "fix" it.

**I measured the RAM figure `redu.md` said nobody publishes:** 114 conversions in 45s at concurrency 2 → peak container RSS **357 MiB** of 3.8 GiB, zero OOM kills, zero restarts. CPU saturated at ~173% of 200% while 3 GB of RAM sat idle. So m1.medium is generous on memory and tight on CPU: go to m1.mem16 to raise *concurrency*, not out of memory pressure, and raise `--chromium-max-concurrency` in the same change.

`redu.md` now carries 4 new quirks, the `last_deploy` block, and a pinned `dname` so a redeploy keeps this URL. Teardown is just `delete_deployment 496` — nothing persists behind it.
